name: Mariners Cave
note: Sea cave reached by an underwater tunnel on boat tours from Neiafu; named as a stop on the day tours and as a dive site.

name: Swallows Cave
note: Sea cave and snorkelling stop on Vava'u boat tours; named as a dive site by Wikivoyage and Tonga Tourism.

name: Swallows Rock
note: Dive site named as one of Vava'u's spectacular dive sites; probably the dive at Swallows Cave, so a near-duplicate, with no coordinates in any source.

name: Mt Talau National Park
note: National park on Utu Vava'u (est. 1995) covering one of the few remaining native forests; trail of about 1 km from 2 km out of Neiafu, with views over the harbour.

name: Mt Talau Lookout
note: Viewpoint at the summit of Mt Talau's walk, with views over Neiafu harbour; part of the Mt Talau National Park walk and so a near-duplicate of it.

name: 'Ene'io Botanical Garden
note: Botanical garden on the east coast of Utu Vava'u with a visitors' centre, tapa and kava; Tonga's only botanical garden.

name: St Joseph's Cathedral, Neiafu
note: Cathedral church in Neiafu, a prominent landmark visible from the harbour, which Wikivoyage lists under See; a church judged on its visitor interest.

name: Utakalongalu Market
note: Traditional market in Neiafu with locally grown fruit and fresh fish; the listing does not say which days it trades.

name: Hunga Island
note: Island 35 minutes from Neiafu with sheltered bays where humpback whales rest with calves; a whale-watching and swimming base in season.

name: Pangaimotu
note: Second-largest island of the group, joined to Utu Vava'u by a land bridge, with beaches, coves and snorkelling.

name: Avai'o'vuna Swamp
note: Small coastal wetland on Pangaimotu named in the Wikivoyage orientation; no coordinates in the source, so a wetland with no listed visitor facilities.

name: Tapana Island
note: Small island ten minutes by boat from Utu Vava'u with a beachfront resort, a Spanish restaurant and fales to stay in; named for the restaurant and the resort.

name: Mala Island
note: Resort island 15 minutes from Neiafu on a 20-acre beach island, known for its Sunday beach pig roast; named for the resort.

name: Mounu Island
note: Islet with a beachfront resort restaurant and bar named in Wikivoyage's Eat list; a resort stop rather than a place to see.

name: Utungake Island
note: Island with beach fale resorts (Tongan Beach Resort and Mystic Sands) listed under Wikivoyage Splurge; accommodation, not an attraction.

name: Blue Lagoon Resort
note: Eco-friendly beach fale resort on Foiata Island, listed under Wikivoyage Splurge; accommodation.

name: Utula'aina Point Lookout
note: Coastal lookout past Holonga on the north of Utu Vava'u, reached on foot; Wikivoyage names it with a walk down to Secret Beach.

name: Secret Beach
note: Beach reached by a hike down from the Utula'aina lookout in the north of Utu Vava'u; no coordinates in the source. (A Wikipedia article named Secret Beach is in Hawaii and was not used.)

name: Toafa Church
note: Church on the west point of Utu Vava'u that Wikivoyage names for its views of the cliffs of Hunga and other islands; a church judged for the view it offers.

name: Vava'u Pearl Centre
note: Mabe pearl centre in Vava'u with a display of pearl information and original pearl designs for sale; a venue for visitors to learn about the pearl.

name: Ava Pulepulekai
note: Fjord-like channel of about 11 km on the south side of the group, named as a Vava'u highlight by Tonga Tourism.

name: Neiafu
note: Town and capital of Vava'u on Utu Vava'u's southern point, the base for tours, yachts and the harbour; the second-largest town in Tonga.

name: Port of Refuge Harbour
note: Sheltered harbour opposite Neiafu, a yacht anchorage and the view from the town; named by Wikivoyage as one of the world's most beautiful harbours.

name: Neiafu Pier
note: Pier across from Coconet where local youth jump off into the harbour, named in Wikivoyage's Do list as a stop.

name: Vanilla Plantations of Utu Vava'u
note: Vanilla farms across Utu Vava'u that Wikivoyage names under See, where vanilla bean growing can be seen; a countryside activity rather than one place.

name: Beluga Diving
note: Dive and whale-watch operator in Vava'u named by Tonga Tourism; an operator, with its base in Neiafu.

name: Kapa Island
note: Small island in the Vava'u group named in the region brief; no visitor source found describing it.

name: Vaka'eitu Island
note: Small island in the Vava'u group named in the region brief; no visitor source found describing it.
